summary.headline: Thyrocare Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 25% YoY to INR271 crore, with a one-time INR45 crore NHL impairment weighing on reported profit.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 25% YoY to INR271 crore and standalone revenue grew 26.7% to INR256 crore, with pathology up 27%. EBITDA margin was 33% and PAT before exceptions rose 26% to INR60 crore. Management is exiting radiology subsidiary Nueclear Healthcare (NHL) by selling it to Trovera for INR141 crore, and booked a non-cash impairment of INR45 crore consolidated (INR9 crore standalone). Management is also launching specialty diagnostics and a pregnancy test kit, both of which are margin-dilutive near term.

financial_highlights.metric: H1 FY27 consolidated revenue / EBITDA / PAT growth

financial_highlights.value: INR45 crore consolidated; INR9 crore standalone
over INR211 crore / zero debt as on 30 Sep 2026

segments.name: Pathology (franchisee)
segments.commentary: Franchisee business grew 27% YoY; about 1,180 franchises added in Q2, the highest quarterly addition in 3 years, taking active base to a record 12,911. Average revenue per franchisee has stayed around INR1.2 lakh per quarter for about 12 quarters.

segments.name: Partnership (B2B)
segments.commentary: Grew 28% YoY, led by insurance and health tech plus existing accounts; PharmEasy is the largest partner at about 11% of the segment. Management said insurance volumes are still small.

segments.name: Specialty diagnostics (allergy, genomics/NIPT)
segments.commentary: Commercially live since May; currently about 4% of pathology revenue. Management targets 10-15% of revenue within 3-5 years.

segments.name: Consumer products (pregnancy kit)
segments.commentary: Launched at MRP INR60 with a INR399 Beta hCG coupon (vs INR800 list). Present in 10,000+ pharmacies via Ascent and PharmEasy; gross margin said to be comparable to diagnostics, but not EPS accretive for at least the next 3 quarters.

segments.name: Radiology (Nueclear Healthcare, NHL)
segments.commentary: Being sold to Trovera for INR141 crore (INR81.9 crore cash plus INR59.5 crore equity), subject to shareholder approval. NHL degrew about 9% over the past 5 quarters, and its ROCE is 6.95% vs Thyrocare's 34.9%.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guidance raised: management now expects early 20s% growth for the full year, versus the earlier mid-teens to high-teens range.
Long-term EBITDA margin guided at about 31-31.5%, with operating leverage reinvested in growth; H1 margin was 32.6%.
Franchisee additions expected at 1,500-2,000 per year; management said Q3 additions will be small and Q4 should return to normal pace.
Specialty and pregnancy-kit investment to continue for at least 3 more quarters; management does not expect EPS accretion from the kit in that period.
Launch expenses of about INR1.5 crore in Q2 and about INR3 crore expected in Q3; ESOP cost about INR4 crore in each of Q1 and Q2.
Capex in H2 FY27 expected to be similar to H1 (about INR30 crore).
Management aims for API Group ex-Thyrocare to turn profitable by Q4 FY27 before any corporate action is considered; the group has no intent to go below 51% in Thyrocare.
capex_capacity: Five new labs added in Q2 (Asansol, Nashik, Madurai, Jabalpur regional processing labs plus a hybrid lab at Jamshedpur); network now 48 labs in India and 1 in Tanzania, versus 49 labs stated in the opening remarks.
H1 FY27 capex of INR30 crore covered new labs and capacity for 27% volume growth; a similar amount is expected in H2.
Specialty capex was made in FY26; testing has started in reproductive genomics (maternal screening) and allergy.
Phlebotomy network of over 2,100; 96% of samples processed in NABL-accredited labs; average turnaround time 3.5 hours.
demand_pricing: Test volume grew 27% YoY, with patients up 13% and tests per patient up 12%, driven by bundling.
Management said the new franchisee base adds at lower revenue per franchisee, so growth is expected mainly from franchisee count rather than revenue per franchisee.
Complaints fell to 2.9 per million tests in Q2, the lowest recorded.
Pregnancy kit: distribution via Ascent (10,000+ chemists), PharmEasy and quick commerce; Yami Gautam is brand ambassador and out-of-home media is planned after Diwali.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q2 franchisee addition surge sustainable, and will FY27 exceed the 1,500 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called Q2 a positive surprise but said Q3 additions will be small and it needs one or two more quarters to confirm a new run rate. It would not confirm exceeding 1,500.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pregnancy kit's supply chain and margin profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Two outsourced vendors assemble the kits to Thyrocare QC standards. Gross margin is comparable to diagnostics and EBITDA is at pathology-like levels, but heavy marketing means no EPS accretion for at least 3 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the NHL sale accompanied by an impairment rather than a gain, given book value of about INR83 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the INR83 crore is only NHL's net worth; the impairment is the gap between the carrying value of the investment (about INR180 crore including goodwill in consolidated books) and the INR141 crore consideration, with the valuation and term sheet triggering it.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins evolve as specialty and devices scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said long-term EBITDA guidance is about 31-31.5%, with investments funded from operating leverage, and that it would not go above that range.

qa_highlights.question: Is a reverse merger or IPO of API Group with Thyrocare under consideration?
qa_highlights.answer: No corporate action is under evaluation. Management set two milestones: API Group debt-free (achieved), and API Group ex-Thyrocare profitable (targeted by Q4 FY27).

qa_highlights.question: Is there any change to revenue guidance, and what is the specialty and consumer mix ambition?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue growth guidance moved to early 20s% for the year, from mid-teens to high-teens. Specialty is targeted at 10-15% of revenue in 3-5 years; management said it is too early to size consumer products.

risks_watch: Franchisee additions may slow in Q3 by management's own account; watch whether Q4 returns to the normal pace.
Margin pressure from specialty, pregnancy-kit marketing and headcount build-out; launch costs are rising (about INR1.5 crore in Q2, about INR3 crore expected in Q3).
Completion of the NHL sale is subject to shareholder approval and SPA execution; the INR45 crore consolidated impairment and treatment of the sale remain open items.
Related-party dependence on the API group distribution network (Ascent, PharmEasy) for the pregnancy kit and partner revenue.
Complaints and service levels: management acknowledged about 1,000 late phlebotomist arrivals per day at 99% on-time performance.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth and franchisee momentum, but measured and deliberately non-committal on forward targets, the pregnancy kit's near-term profitability and any API group corporate action. Management repeatedly said it would wait for milestones before giving more guidance.
key_quotes: Continuing the growth momentum of over 20% achieved in each of the past 2 years, our pathology business grew even faster in Q2 FY27, delivering 27% growth.
So I do not anticipate this being EPS accretive at least for the next 3 quarters, right, because we will do a lot of out-of-home media.
I have guided to API Group ex-Thyrocare turning profitable by Q4 FY27.

growth.why: Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to early 20s% (midpoint ~21%) from mid-to-high teens, backed by franchisee adds (~1,180 in Q2, 1,500-2,000 p.a. target), test volume growth of 27%, and H1 capex of INR30 crore for new labs and capacity for 27% volume growth, with a similar H2 spend; Q3 franchisee adds are expected to be small.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Long-term EBITDA margin is guided at 31-31.5% versus H1 at 32.6%, with specialty, pregnancy-kit marketing and headcount build-out reinvesting operating leverage; the pregnancy kit is not EPS accretive for at least 3 quarters.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Five new labs commissioned in Q2 (48 labs in India, 1 in Tanzania) and H1 capex of INR30 crore covered capacity for 27% volume growth, with a similar INR30 crore in H2; franchisee base at a record 12,911 adds 1,500-2,000 per year.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Test volume grew 27% YoY (patients up 13%, tests per patient up 12%), Q2 added about 1,180 franchisees (highest in 3 years), and the 1,500-2,000 annual addition target is held.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed, so the capex call rests on the guided H2 spend of about INR30 crore being similar to H1, which is a run-rate plan rather than a new capacity announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guidance was already raised to early 20s% (midpoint ~21%) against H1 growth of 25%, and management called Q2 franchisee adds a positive surprise, though it would not confirm exceeding 1,500.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management just raised FY27 revenue growth to early 20s% from mid-to-high teens, and H1 revenue grew 25% with EBITDA up 29%; the only soft spots flagged are Q3 franchisee adds and launch costs of about INR3 crore in Q3.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Pregnancy kit is already launched at MRP INR60 across 10,000+ pharmacies, with out-of-home media planned after Diwali, and specialty diagnostics (allergy, reproductive genomics) is commercially live since May at about 4% of pathology revenue.

rows.label: NHL radiology sale to Trovera for INR141 crore
rows.why: Consideration is INR81.9 crore cash plus INR59.5 crore equity, subject to shareholder approval and SPA execution; NHL degrew about 9% over 5 quarters with ROCE of 6.95%, and the INR45 crore consolidated impairment is booked.

rows.label: API Group ex-Thyrocare profitable milestone
rows.why: Management targets API Group ex-Thyrocare profitability by Q4 FY27 before any corporate action, and says the group will not go below 51% in Thyrocare; no corporate action is under evaluation.

rows.label: Pregnancy kit EPS dilution
rows.why: Heavy marketing with launch costs of about INR1.5 crore in Q2 and about INR3 crore in Q3 means the kit is not EPS accretive for at least the next 3 quarters, even though gross margin is comparable to diagnostics.

tone.note: Management was confident on test volume growth, franchisee momentum and the raised early-20s% revenue guide, but non-committal on the pregnancy kit's near-term profit, the API Group corporate action and whether Q2's franchisee surge holds; analysts pressed on those sustainability and margin question
